exam_name: Microsoft Azure AI Cloud Developer Associate

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Which Azure resource type provides a single endpoint and key to access multiple Azure AI services (language, vision, speech) together?

options.A: Azure AI Services multi-service resource

questions.explanation: The Azure AI Services multi-service resource gives one endpoint/key covering several cognitive capabilities, simplifying provisioning versus creating a separate resource per service.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Which Azure service is the primary hub for building, training, and deploying custom machine learning models?

options.A: Azure Machine Learning

questions.explanation: Azure Machine Learning is Microsoft's managed platform for the full ML lifecycle: data prep, training, hyperparameter tuning, and deployment.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Azure role-based access control (RBAC) is used to:

options.A: Grant specific permissions on Azure resources to users, groups, or service principals

questions.explanation: RBAC assigns roles (with defined permission sets) to security principals scoped to a subscription, resource group, or resource, controlling who can do what.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Which Azure feature lets you keep API keys and connection strings out of application code?

options.A: Azure Key Vault

questions.explanation: Azure Key Vault securely stores secrets, keys, and certificates, which applications retrieve at runtime instead of hardcoding them.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A resource group in Azure is best described as:

options.A: A logical container that holds related Azure resources for a solution

questions.explanation: Resource groups organise resources that share a lifecycle, making it easier to manage, deploy, and delete them together.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Which pricing consideration is unique to consuming a large language model via an Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI deployment?

options.A: Cost is typically based on the number of input and output tokens processed
options.B: Cost is always a flat monthly fee regardless of usage
options.C: Cost depends only on the number of developers on the team
options.D: There is no cost associated with model usage

questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI/Foundry model usage is commonly billed per token consumed (input plus output), so cost scales with prompt and response length and call volume.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: Azure AI Foundry (formerly Azure AI Studio) is primarily used to:

options.A: Build, evaluate, and deploy generative AI applications, including model selection and orchestration

questions.explanation: Azure AI Foundry provides a unified environment for exploring models, building prompt flows/agents, evaluating outputs, and deploying generative AI solutions.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: In an Azure OpenAI chat completion request, the "system" message is used to:

options.A: Set the assistant's behaviour, role, and constraints for the conversation

questions.explanation: The system message establishes persona and instructions the model should follow throughout the chat, distinct from user and assistant turn messages.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: The "temperature" parameter in an Azure OpenAI completion request controls:

options.A: The randomness/creativity of the generated output

questions.explanation: Temperature adjusts sampling randomness; lower values produce more deterministic, focused output, higher values produce more varied output.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: "Prompt engineering" refers to:

options.A: Designing and refining the input text given to a model to elicit better outputs

questions.explanation: Prompt engineering iteratively crafts instructions, examples, and context in the prompt to improve the quality and reliability of model responses.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: Fine-tuning a model on Azure OpenAI is used to:

options.A: Adapt a base model's behaviour using additional training examples specific to a task or domain
options.B: Change the Azure subscription's billing region
options.C: Increase the virtual machine's disk size

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning continues training a base model on custom labelled examples so it better follows a specific style, format, or domain behaviour.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: Which is a valid reason to use function calling / tool calling with an Azure OpenAI model?

options.A: To let the model request structured invocation of an external function or API to fetch data or perform an action
options.C: To reduce the Azure bill to zero

questions.explanation: Function/tool calling lets the model emit a structured call (with arguments) that the application executes, extending the model beyond pure text generation.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: An "agent" in the context of Azure AI Foundry Agent Service is best described as:

options.A: An AI-powered component that can reason, plan, and call tools to complete multi-step tasks

questions.explanation: Agents combine an LLM with tools, memory, and orchestration logic to autonomously work through multi-step tasks rather than answering a single prompt.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: Which Azure service is commonly used to orchestrate multi-step workflows that call AI models, APIs, and other Azure services in sequence?

options.A: Azure Logic Apps or Azure Durable Functions

questions.explanation: Logic Apps and Durable Functions provide orchestration primitives (steps, branching, state) suited to coordinating multi-step AI-driven workflows or agent action sequences.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: "Grounding" an agent's tool call in real data (rather than letting it hallucinate the answer) typically involves:

options.A: Connecting the agent to an external data source, API, or knowledge base it can query for facts
options.B: Increasing the model's temperature to maximum
options.D: Disconnecting the agent from the internet entirely

questions.explanation: Grounding connects the model to authoritative external data (via tools, RAG, or plugins) so its answers are based on retrieved facts rather than invented content.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: Which is a basic safeguard for an agent that can call tools with side effects (like sending an email or making a payment)?

options.A: Requiring explicit confirmation or human approval before executing high-impact actions
options.B: Giving the agent unrestricted access to every API with no limits
options.C: Removing all logging of the agent's actions
options.D: Allowing the agent to modify its own permissions freely

questions.explanation: Human-in-the-loop confirmation for consequential actions is a basic safety pattern preventing an agent from taking irreversible actions autonomously without oversight.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Azure AI Search (formerly Azure Cognitive Search) is primarily used to:

options.A: Index and search content, including vector-based similarity search over embeddings

questions.explanation: Azure AI Search indexes documents and supports full-text and vector search, a common backbone for RAG-based grounding of generative AI applications.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: In a RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) pipeline on Azure, the retrieval step typically:

options.A: Finds relevant document chunks from an index (such as Azure AI Search) to include as context for the model

questions.explanation: Retrieval fetches the most relevant stored content for the user's query, which is then passed to the generation model as grounding context.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: An "embedding model" deployed via Azure OpenAI is used to:

options.A: Convert text into a numeric vector representing its meaning, for similarity search

questions.explanation: Embedding models output vectors capturing semantic meaning, enabling similarity comparisons used in vector search and RAG retrieval.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: "Chunking" a document before indexing for RAG refers to:

options.A: Splitting the document into smaller passages so relevant sections can be retrieved individually

questions.explanation: Chunking breaks long documents into manageable, semantically coherent pieces so retrieval can return focused, relevant context rather than entire documents.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Azure AI Document Intelligence (formerly Form Recognizer) is used to:

options.A: Extract structured data (text, tables, key-value pairs) from documents such as invoices or forms

questions.explanation: Document Intelligence uses AI models to pull structured information out of scanned or digital documents, useful as a data-preparation step for knowledge mining.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Azure AI Content Safety is used to:

options.A: Detect and filter harmful content such as hate speech, violence, or self-harm in text and images

questions.explanation: Content Safety analyses content for categories of harm and returns severity scores, letting applications filter or flag unsafe generated or user-submitted content.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Which is a core pillar commonly cited in Microsoft's Responsible AI principles?

options.A: Fairness
options.C: Fastest possible response time regardless of accuracy

questions.explanation: Microsoft's Responsible AI principles include fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Managed identities in Azure are used so that an application can:

options.A: Authenticate to other Azure services without storing credentials in code or configuration

questions.explanation: A managed identity gives an Azure resource an automatically-managed identity for Azure AD authentication, removing the need to embed secrets for service-to-service calls.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Private endpoints in Azure are used to:

options.A: Allow a service to be accessed over a private IP within a virtual network instead of the public internet
options.C: Reduce the number of tokens used per request

questions.explanation: Private endpoints connect a virtual network privately to a service (like Azure OpenAI), keeping traffic off the public internet for improved security.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: "Data residency" concerns in an Azure AI solution relate to:

options.A: Which geographic region data is stored and processed in, for compliance reasons
options.C: The colour scheme of the admin portal
options.D: The number of parameters in the model

questions.explanation: Regulatory and compliance requirements often mandate that data stay within specific geographic or legal boundaries, influencing Azure region selection.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Azure Container Apps or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) would typically be used to:

options.A: Host and scale containerised application workloads, including AI service wrappers

questions.explanation: Container Apps and AKS are compute platforms for running containerised applications, commonly used to host APIs or microservices that call AI models.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Azure Functions is best suited for:

options.A: Running small, event-driven pieces of code without managing the underlying server infrastructure

questions.explanation: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service for short-lived, event-triggered code, a common choice for lightweight AI pipeline steps or webhooks.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Application Insights (part of Azure Monitor) is used to:

options.A: Collect telemetry such as requests, exceptions, and performance metrics from an application

questions.explanation: Application Insights instruments an app to capture requests, dependencies, exceptions, and custom metrics, enabling monitoring and diagnostics.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Which metric would you monitor to track the cost efficiency of an Azure OpenAI-based feature?

options.A: Tokens consumed per request and total token spend over time
options.B: The number of CSS files loaded

questions.explanation: Since billing is typically token-based, tracking tokens per request and aggregate token spend is central to monitoring and optimising cost.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: "Provisioned throughput units" (PTUs) in Azure OpenAI provide:

options.A: Reserved, predictable model capacity for consistent latency and throughput, as an alternative to standard pay-as-you-go
options.C: A discount on storage costs only

questions.explanation: PTUs reserve dedicated model capacity, giving predictable performance for high-volume or latency-sensitive workloads compared with shared standard deployments.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Autoscaling an Azure App Service or Container App is used to:

options.A: Automatically adjust the number of running instances based on load
options.D: Translate the application into another language

questions.explanation: Autoscaling rules add or remove instances based on metrics (CPU, queue length, request rate), helping the service handle variable demand cost-effectively.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Infrastructure as Code (IaC), such as Bicep or Terraform, is used in an Azure AI solution to:

options.A: Define and provision infrastructure through versioned, repeatable code rather than manual portal clicks

questions.explanation: IaC tools let teams declare infrastructure in code, enabling repeatable, version-controlled, and auditable deployments across environments.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A "vector index" stores:

options.A: Numeric embedding vectors that can be searched for nearest neighbours by similarity
options.B: Only plain text with no numeric representation

questions.explanation: A vector index organises embeddings for efficient approximate nearest-neighbour search, the core mechanism behind semantic/vector search.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A "jailbreak" attempt against a deployed AI application refers to:

options.A: A user crafting input to bypass the system's safety instructions or content policies

questions.explanation: Jailbreak prompts try to trick the model into ignoring its guardrails; defending against them is part of responsible AI implementation.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: The "max tokens" parameter in a completion request controls:

options.A: The maximum length of the model's generated response
options.B: The number of users allowed to call the API

questions.explanation: Max tokens caps how many tokens the model may generate in its response, useful for controlling output length and cost.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Caching frequent, identical AI model responses is a technique primarily used to:

options.A: Reduce latency and cost by avoiding repeated calls to the model for the same input

questions.explanation: Caching avoids redundant model calls for repeated identical (or near-identical) requests, cutting both latency and token cost.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Which is a valid reason to choose a smaller, cheaper model for a given AI feature instead of the largest available model?

options.A: The task is simple enough that a smaller model meets quality requirements at lower cost and latency
options.B: Smaller models are always more accurate for every task
options.C: Smaller models never need any evaluation
options.D: Smaller models cannot be deployed on Azure

questions.explanation: Model selection should match task complexity; using a smaller, cheaper, faster model where sufficient avoids overpaying for unneeded capability.
